newsitem.title: USA: MBL Life Assurance says adjusted capital rose.
newsitem.headline: MBL Life Assurance says adjusted capital rose.

text.p: MBL Life Assurance Corp said Wednesday its total adjusted capital rose by $48 million during the first three months of 1997, to $442 million.

The figure also exceeded the company's total adjusted capital of $278 million at the same point in 1996. Total adjusted capital, the sum of the company's surplus and asset valuation reserve, is a measurement of an insurer's net worth.
MBL assumed and reinsured the insurance liabilities and most of the assets Mutual Benefit Life Insurance Co in May 1994, when a court-approved rehabilitation plan was put in place.

The plan is in effect through the end of 1999, during which time MBL Life is rebuilding its capital base and shifting its invested asset profile from real estate assets to investment-grade corporate bonds.

"We hope that the strengthening of our investment portfolio, our lower cost structure and the significant benefits achieved in the settlement of very material litigation will help to restore our policyholders' confidence in the financial viability of MBL Life," MBL president Alan Bowers said in a statement.
